archetype.name: Field General (short-area distributor)
archetype.definition: A veteran who has traded much of his off-script downfield risk for timing throws, under-center play action and quick decisions that keep the offense on schedule and the sack total low.

report.headline: A safer, sack-proof Mahomes is winning, but the passing game is drifting.
report.take:
This is a different Mahomes from the one in the career table. His aggressiveness (throws into tight windows) has fallen to 6.81% from 13.3% last year. His intended air yards sit at 6.25 and his rushing has dropped to 11.8 yards a game from 30.1. In exchange he has become one of the hardest quarterbacks in the league to sack. His 3.5% sack rate ranks 4th of 45, and only 17.6% of his pressures end in sacks (6th), after 28.8% last season ranked 28th. The ball is coming out on time, and that is the defining change of his 2026.

The efficiency comes from a narrow base. Travis Kelce is producing 0.555 EPA per target on 35 looks, and throws of 10-19 air yards return 0.423 EPA per play. Tyquan Thornton has turned 15 targets into 19.0 EPA, nearly matching Kelce's total on less than half the volume. The offense also leans on Andy Reid's run game, which is first in rushing EPA. Mahomes is far better under center (0.239 EPA per play) than in shotgun (0.072). Add a defense ranked 5th and you get a 5-1 record built on complementary football, not on him carrying the team.

The five-game line flatters him. The 0.147 EPA per dropback over the last five games is propped up by Weeks 2 and 3 (13.4 and 12.9 EPA). The last three games have come in at -0.016 per dropback, with a -2.5 CPOE and two touchdowns. That stretch includes a 0-TD, 272-yard game against the Chargers and a 165-yard, -6.0 EPA loss in Seattle. The deep ball is not working: 33.3% completions, a -6.2 CPOE, two interceptions and no touchdowns on 21 attempts. Outside Kelce and Thornton, Xavier Worthy and Kenneth Walker III have each taken more than 25 targets at negative EPA. Thornton's rate is a few big plays, not a repeatable baseline, so the passing offense's floor is thinner than its season average suggests.

The immediate picture is harder. Starting tackle Jaylon Moore (89% of snaps) and Rashee Rice are both listed out, Josh Simmons is on IR, and the next opponent is a Denver defense that ranks 2nd in hit rate. The quick-release style is exactly what protects a patched line, so expect it to hold. The open question is whether he can reopen the intermediate and deep game enough to lift the scoring back toward the early weeks. Until he does, this is a quarterback who is above league average and in the middle of the qualifier pack.

strengths.title: Pressure no longer turns into sacks
strengths.body: Only 17.6% of his pressures become sacks, down from 28.8% last year, and his sack rate is 4th-lowest among qualifiers. That comes from a deliberate shift to shorter, earlier throws, visible in the halved aggressiveness rate, not from a sudden change in pocket feel. As long as the scheme stays this conservative it should hold, and it matters more with two tackles unavailable.

strengths.title: Kelce and the intermediate middle
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards have been his best area at 0.423 EPA per play, and Kelce is the main reason. He is drawing a top-share 35 targets at 0.555 EPA each. That is a long-standing connection, not a hot streak, so it is the most bankable part of the passing game. The risk is concentration: if Kelce is bracketed, the next-best volume options have been negative.

strengths.title: Play action off a top run game
strengths.body: Under center he posts 0.239 EPA per play and a 7.8 CPOE, against 0.072 from shotgun. That is the payoff of an offense that ranks 1st in rushing EPA. His 12 scrambles have also been efficient at 0.406 EPA each, even with fewer rushing yards overall. This structure is scheme-driven and should travel week to week.

concerns.title: Three-game slide in production
concerns.body: Over Weeks 4-7 his EPA per dropback fell to -0.016 and his TD rate to 2.2%. The low point was -6.0 EPA at Seattle, the league's 2nd-ranked defense. Part of that is opponents, and the Las Vegas game came with 33.3% pressure. But the Chargers game produced 272 yards and no scores, a sign the short game is moving the ball without finishing drives. With Rice out and Worthy and Walker producing negative EPA per target, there is little outside Kelce to pull him out of it.

concerns.title: The deep ball has gone missing
concerns.body: On 20+ air-yard throws he is 33.3% with a -6.2 CPOE, two interceptions and no touchdowns. That is a real flaw so far, not a cost of a strength. His career efficiency was built on hitting these, so some recovery is likely. But 21 attempts is a small sample, and the conservative approach means fewer chances to fix it.

concerns.title: Safe throws fall short on third
concerns.body: His average throw lands 2.27 yards short of the sticks, and the team converts only 34% on third down, where four of his seven sacks have come. This is the direct price of the low-risk approach. It is sustainable as a style but caps drive success against good defenses.

trend.note: He peaked in Weeks 2-3 with back-to-back double-digit EPA games, then slid to 1.7, 2.8 and -6.0. Better opponents explain part of the dip, but the short passing game has stopped producing points.

nextGame.headline: Denver's pass rush meets a patched line; Kelce is the release.
nextGame.body:
Denver's defense ranks 4th in EPA and 4th against the pass, with the 2nd-best hit rate and the 6th-stingiest deep defense. That runs straight into his two soft spots: downfield throws and a weakened tackle group. The Week 1 meeting is the template. He finished at -2.3 EPA with a -11.9 CPOE and a 20% bad-throw rate, and Kansas City still won 31-10 on defense and the ground game. The opening is on the ground: Denver ranks 26th against the run and 28th in explosive runs allowed, and offenses lean on the run against it. That suits Kansas City's top-ranked rushing offense and the under-center play action where he is sharpest.

Availability cuts both ways, and several key players are listed out with an estimated return of game day itself, so treat them as real question marks. On his side, starting tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) and Rashee Rice (hamstring) are listed out, and Josh Simmons is on IR. That puts a premium on his quick release and leaves Kelce and Thornton as the main options. On Denver's side, cornerback Pat Surtain II (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga are both listed out, and edge Zach Allen is questionable. If Surtain and Hufanga sit, the intermediate and deep windows open noticeably, and losing Allen would ease the pressure concern. The Book has Kansas City as a 1.5-point favorite with a 41.5 total, which points to a low-scoring, field-position game.

keyMatchups.title: Pass rush versus backup tackles
keyMatchups.body: Denver gets hits on 21.6% of dropbacks, 2nd in the league. Moore, an 89%-snap starter, is listed out. Mahomes' sack avoidance is built for this, but it tends to push him toward checkdowns and away from shot plays. Allen's hamstring status could shift this significantly.

keyMatchups.title: Kelce against a leaky TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Denver allows 0.46 EPA per target to opposing top tight ends, 29th of 32, while Kelce is producing 0.555 per target. With Rice likely out and Hufanga possibly missing from the back end, Kelce is the clearest path to efficient throws.

keyMatchups.title: Run-first script favors play action
keyMatchups.body: Denver is soft against the run, and offenses already tilt run-heavy against it. Kansas City has the league's best rushing EPA. If the ground game works, his under-center dropbacks, his best split, should get cleaner looks. It also lowers his pass volume.

nextGame.watch: Whether he attacks the 10-19 yard middle and takes deep shots if Surtain and Hufanga sit, or stays in the checkdown mode of the last three weeks.

restOfSeason.body:
The structure looks durable: a low sack rate, a strong run game, a top-five defense and a quarterback who has chosen to play under control. That points to a solid efficiency floor and plenty of wins, but modest volume. Expect something like 225-265 passing yards and 1.2-1.8 touchdowns a game, with the rushing well below his 2025 level. Thornton's per-target production will come down, and the red-zone touchdowns have come on low-EPA plays. Some of the scoring is fragile.

The upside lever is the deep ball. His career says the 33.3% completion rate and -6.2 CPOE on deep throws should improve, and some of the turnovers there were bad luck on few throws. If Rice returns healthy and the tackles stabilize, the efficiency should drift back toward the early-season level. If the line stays thin, the passing offense will keep looking like the last three weeks against good defenses. His interception rate sits near league average, which fits his career, where turnovers have usually been part of the package.
swingFactors: Health of the tackle group (Moore, Simmons)
Rashee Rice's return from the hamstring injury
Whether the deep ball and aggressiveness come back

confidence.note: Six games, a clear stylistic shift, plus offensive-line and receiver injuries clouding the near term.
